top_choice_rationale: P001 credits Katori and Ye for the optical lattice clock, a specific invention (magic-wavelength lattice removing the trap light shift while keeping Lamb-Dicke confinement, with many atoms interrogated at once) that is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. It is confirmed in the way I ask of any claim: Sr, Yb and Hg clocks in several countries agree at the low 1e-18 level. It has already measured something about nature (millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, bounds on varying constants), and the two-name credit is the cleanest on the slate. The citation is scoped to the lattice clock only, so Ye's comb work is not re-credited. Priority dates and uncertainty values still need checking against the record. P002 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) is a respectable second: the science is strong, but the credit chain is contested (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu, Hasan) and I cannot judge it as well as my condensed-matter colleagues. No award is last because two mature, defensible proposals are available.
recusal_note: No conflict for P001 or P002 apparent from profile: no known tie to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp. I am a member of the PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations, and neutrino astronomy (B033) is close to my own field, but it is not on the slate.
